The Boundary Chart

Mathematics in James boundary arithmetic, one law per step, from the void toward F₁. Every law is drawn, glossed, derived from the laws before it, and checked by the engine. Built so far: rungs void, N, Z, mult, Q, alg and C — the classical James algebra of the 1993 thesis (Chapters 4–6 and Appendix B, checked against the text) with the standard complex-number toolkit — schema, the laws over every n (cardinality, powers, the n-th roots of unity, De Moivre) stated once as templates, checked at every n in a range, and priced with the induction gap they lean on; and J1, the enriched calculus 𝕁₁ — Involution split into a strict counit and a witnessed unit, the log of one kept as the period form ω rather than erased, every step graded by the receipt it posts (strict, absorbed, posted) by the receipt prover, James's two theorems of Chapter 6 re-read as true mod Λ, and the ψ-wall counting 24, 240, 504; and place, the finite places — a place is a pile declared void, the page at p read in its log space (a number part, a count of the prime's log, a count of the torsion log), the same wall (ω A) ≃ (A) with the place's own period, every trunk law read at p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 13 and every derivation re-graded there, Fermat and Hensel and the doll of 1/(1 − p) as laws, and the ψ-wall split into its local factors.

void.spaceprimitiveNATIVEengineshape-ledband Kmedium●

Space — juxtaposition is unordered

≐
A B ≐ B AA B ≐ A Ba + b = b + a

Things sitting together on a page have no first or second; so adding is the same in either order, for free.

classical holdsJ1 holdsJH holdsJO holdsJP holdsC EXACTfinset EXACTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic EXACT
Derivation

none — adjoined. A fact of the medium; its unit is the void, void.page.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The additive layer of arithmetic is a commutative monoid with the void as unit — before any number has been written. It is not multiplication: juxtaposition becomes multiplication only under an instance boundary, ([A][B]), at mult.multiplication. And it is the deepest design decision in the calculus: because breadth is unordered, no non-commutative product can ever live in it (the No-Go theorem, JH-1 — a later node).

The natural numbers as unary numerals: every n ≥ 1 is a pile, and 0 is the void (void.page). This is not positional notation — the calculus has no base — and it is not Laws of Form: there o o ≐ o (the law of Calling), so LoF has no natural numbers. James's refusal of Calling is where number begins.

Refuted readings

  • "nothing added later ever collapses two piles" follows from soundness in ℂ — the first draft (2026-10-03) made this claim here with an engine badge; the referee pass the same day showed the unrestricted laws do collapse the calculus unless the undefined forms are excluded, and that nothing in the engine checks a meta claim. Moved to mult.consistency, with its decree and import made explicit.

Notes

The witness tools/models/freeness_check.py enumerates piles up to twelve units and confirms their canonical forms are pairwise distinct — all that a fragment with no rewrite rules can be asked to show.

The JP cell is the first place the chart shows the place calculus doing something to ℕ rather than with it: the void pile p^N ≐ void is a decree that breaks this theorem on purpose. That is a feature of the chart, not a bug of either calculus.

N.inductiongapABSENThandmetaneed-ledband beyondconcept◐

Induction on a pile

GAP — 'a law that holds of void and is preserved by adjoining o holds of every pile' is not a form and not an equation
P(0) ∧ (∀n. P(n) ⇒ P(n+1)) ⇒ ∀n. P(n)

The calculus can show something for 2, for 3, for 4 — one pile at a time — but it has no way to say "and so on, forever."

classical failsJ1 failsJH failsJO failsJP failsC ABSENTfinset PARTIALlambda untestedCC untestedlogic ABSENT
Derivation

none — gap.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That James's calculus is an equational theory of forms, not a logic: it has no quantifiers, no implication, no variables ranging over properties. Every "for all n" in the chart is a meta-statement the reader supplies: a kind: instance node states one value of such a family, and a schema node (rung schema, SPEC §2.7) states the family as a template, checked by the engine at every value in a declared range and closed by a hypothesis row that cites this gap — so from rung schema on the gap is priced (it appears in the price of every schema and of everything built on one) rather than merely named. That is the Plan's option (i), the schema as an admissible rule of the chart's proof language, taken in its weakest form: the engine checks the base case and that the hypothesis row is the law at a smaller parameter; the passage to all n it cannot check, and does not claim to. The two ends of the chart both need this gap closed: the Lean expansion (where Nat.rec is native) and the F₁ end (where ℕ must be recognized as the free commutative monoid on o).

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That order is meta in James's calculus: it is read off normal forms, exactly as it is read off tallies. The boundary-analysis thread (2026-09-29 → 10-01) found the same: order is native on piles but needs a free choice of base for general forms, pinned by the derivative. Trichotomy, the triangle inequality and the metric all wait on this gap.

The chart's own equality field is this axiom's shadow: ≐ classical, ≡/≃ in J1 where the unit is weakened.

The depth-1 criterion (J1). A Λ-sensitive step — the unit [(X)] ≐ X in either direction, or [o] ≐ void — that sits at depth 1 under an instance boundary, passing only through angle boundaries on the way (which carry −λ ∈ Λ), is absorbed by that instance (A5′: (λ A) ≐ (A) for λ ∈ Λ), so a law whose Λ-steps are all of that kind holds exactly in J1 even though each step holds only mod Λ. The slogan "both sides under an instance" is neither necessary nor sufficient: Q.fractional-cardinality has a bare A on one side and is exact (its last step is the strict counit), while ([ [(X)] Y ]) ≐ ([X Y]) has both sides under an instance and fails (the Λ-step sits at depth 2, under a square). The Q-rung J1 cells cite this note.

Confirms

ln 1 = 0 — the log of the multiplicative unit is the additive unit. Every use of "[o] ≐ void" on the chart (the unit law ([A][o]) ≐ A, every removal of a count of one, every [o] → void inside a power) is this law and nothing else, so it is a node of its own rather than a line in mult.unit-law. It is not a free fact: it is one unit step, at void content — and in J1 that step is exactly the one that is weakened. There [()] is not void but the period form ω, and [()] ≃ void holds only with the receipt ω: this law is the classical shadow of the lattice. (The engine's seam check exempts the unit at void content from the decree because the classical reading makes it exact, ln 1 = 0 — SPEC §5.4; it is not a theorem of the hole rules, and the 𝕁₁ reading, in which the log of exactly one is ω, keeps every hole rule and falsifies it.)

Confirms

The ring theorem a · 0 = 0, and its standard proof: a·0 = a·(0+0) = a·0 + a·0, then subtract a·0. The subtraction is the step the calculus cannot do without the angle boundary — Distribution alone only gives (A []) ≐ (A []) (A []), an idempotent, which is not void in every model (mult.dominion-independence). So "times zero is zero" costs Inversion. That is why absorption is an axiom of semirings — it does not follow from the other semiring laws — and a theorem of rings; the chart's price ledger shows the same fact as a cost.

Notes

Against the thesis: James's Theorem 2 (Ch. 4 §4.4.1, p. 28) proves Dominion as □A = [(□A)] = □, "from void multiplication with an involution", and void multiplication ([a][]) = void (p. 26) by the argument that ([a][])([a][]) = ([a][]) by Distribution and "the equation ee = e is true when e is void or when collection of e is idempotent. Since collection is assumed additive, ee ≠ e unless e is void." That assumption — collection has no idempotents — is outside the three axioms, and it is exactly what the independence witness violates: in the 3-element model of mult.dominion-independence the element 1 satisfies 1 + 1 = 1. The chart's derivation routes instead through mult.zero-annihilates, i.e. through Inversion, which James's two-boundary calculus does not yet have.

Whether James's own thesis proof routes through Inversion is to be checked against the 1993 text; Bricken's Iconic Arithmetic presentations sometimes take Dominion as an axiom, which the independence result explains. The engine's shadow check of the law itself evaluates □ A as □ by its own rule — i.e. by this law — so the evidence for the law is the derivation, not the check; the check guards the derivation's steps.

Without the mirror, the page cannot prove that the bottomless pit swallows everything; here is a tiny toy world where it doesn't.

classical holdsJ1 untestedJH untestedJO untestedJP holdsC EXACTfinset untestedlambda untestedCC untestedlogic untested
Derivation
statementrulenote
A model of the medium plus Involution and Distribution is a commutative monoid (M, +, 0) — the multiset syntax forces commutativity and associativity — with a bijection e : M → M (the round boundary), l = e⁻¹ (the square), satisfying e(a + l(b + c)) = e(a + l b) + e(a + l c) for all a, b, c; the angle boundary may be interpreted by any map, since no axiom of this fragment constrains itvoid.space mult.involution mult.distributionany equational derivation is sound in any such total algebra
Take M = {0, 1, 2} with 0 the unit, 1 + 1 = 1, 1 + 2 = 1, 2 + 2 = 2; e(0) = 2, e(1) = 1, e(2) = 0—the witness; tools/models/dominion_models.py checks all 27 instances of Distribution
In this model □ = l(0) = 2 ≠ 0 = void, and (□) = e(2) = 0 = void as mult.hole-instance requires — but □ + 1 = 2 + 1 = 1 ≠ 2, so □ A ≐ □ fails at A = 1—hence mult.dominion is not derivable from the two axioms
M is not a group (1 has no inverse), so Z.inversion has no interpretation here — consistent with the derivation of mult.zero-annihilates and mult.dominion through Inversion—the other two axioms do not suffice; with Inversion (by those nodes) they do

The script also reports the census of labelled structures (not isomorphism classes): of all commutative monoids of order ≤ 4 with a bijection satisfying Distribution, Dominion fails in 1 of 2 (order 2), 4 of 8 (order 3), 42 of 78 (order 4); those counts include degenerate models with □ = void, and only the chosen witness insists on □ ≠ void. (□) ≐ void holds in every model, as it must — it is Involution at 0 (mult.hole-instance).

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That James's three axioms are not redundant for this theorem: the additive-inverse axiom is what makes zero absorbing, exactly as in algebra at large — absorption (0·a = 0) must be postulated in a semiring because it does not follow from distributivity and the monoid laws, and is derived in a ring. The witness model is itself such a structure: a commutative pre-semiring with unit e(0) = 2 in which 0·1 = 1. The shape of the fact is textbook; what this node adds is the James-specific witness, with the exp/log bijection in place, showing where in the chart the cost falls.

James's own proof of Dominion (p. 28, via void multiplication p. 26) assumes that "collection is additive" — no element is idempotent, ee ≠ e unless e is void. The witness model has 1 + 1 = 1: it is a model of Involution and Distribution in which collection is not additive, and Dominion fails. So the independence result locates James's hidden assumption exactly; with Inversion in hand (Ch. 5) the assumption is unnecessary, as mult.zero-annihilates shows.

The two undefined forms

You may not mirror the bottomless pit, and you may not ask what you would have to circle to get it. Both questions have no answer, and the page refuses them rather than answering wrongly.

classical holdsJ1 holdsJH holdsJO holdsJP holdsC EXACTfinset ABSENTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic untested
Derivation

none — adjoined, as a decree about the two forms built from Z.angle, mult.square and mult.black-hole. The calculus does not derive the exclusion; it legislates it, and the legislation is load-bearing. If <□> were admitted, Dominion and Inversion would give A ≐ A □ <□> ≐ □ <□> ≐ void for every A. If [□] were admitted, write W for (o [□]): Dominion inside the square gives (o [□]) ≐ (o [□ C]), Distribution gives (o [□ C]) ≐ (o [□]) (o [C]), so W ≐ W X with X = (o [C]); adjoining <W> and cancelling gives X ≐ void, i.e. (o [C]) ≐ void for every C, and with C = (<o>) the unit itself is void. Either admission makes every form equal to every other.

What the decree protects is the consistency of the whole calculus (mult.consistency): the engine enforces it by raising Excluded and Undefined whenever a derivation row evaluates to one of the two forms, which is the up-to-value version of the rule.

The seam discipline

DISCIPLINE — a unit step, in either orientation ([(X)] → X or X → [(X)]), is admissible only when X lies on the principal strip in the ℂ reading (−π < Im X ≤ π), or when the redex is in an absorbing position: directly inside an instance boundary, through angle boundaries at most

none — adjoined, as a decree about the unit direction of mult.involution, stated in terms of mult.square, Z.angle, N.round, position in space void.space, and the ℂ reading mult.c-reading. The collapse it is legislated against is recorded under Notes.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

James's own repair of the "crack" in his calculus (Ch. 6 §6.3, p. 47): J-cancellation permitted only inside an instance boundary, and only after other reductions — constraints he himself calls "not exhaustive". The chart states a stronger rule one rung earlier, and semantically — James's two J-rules sit inside it as special cases (C.james-discipline) — because the collapse can be written as soon as [<o>] or [[[oo]]] can — at rung mult, before J is a named form — and because no syntactic signature of "off the strip" is available in the calculus (the witness [[[oo]]] refutes the natural one). Soundness under the decree is the theorem mult.consistency. JH's seam guard — [(A)] → A only when L(exp V(A)) = V(A) — is the same rule; J1's answer is different in kind: it does not refuse the step, it prices it with a receipt, and the depth-1 criterion (mult.involution, Notes) says when the price is absorbed.

Refuted readings

  • the guard need only cover the orientation [(X)] → X — the first statement of this decree (2026-10-03); refuted the same day by the alg referee pass: the collapse runs backwards through X → [(X)] (Notes).
  • the pilot's rungs need no guard on Involution-down; the J-discipline is rung C's business — refuted 2026-10-03 (second referee pass): J J = [<o>][<o>] is writable at rung mult, and the collapse above uses only rungs ≤ Q.
  • "phased" — a square with an angle somewhere inside it — is a sufficient syntactic signature for off-strip content, so the decree can be stated in forms alone — refuted the same day by the consistency witness (tools/models/consistency_check.py): [[[oo]]] = ln(ln ln 2) has imaginary part π with no angle anywhere, and [[[oo]]] [[[oo]]] is off the strip. Sign is lost under iterated squares, not only under mirrors; which iterated squares lose it depends on values ([[ooo]] is positive, [[oo]] negative). The decree is therefore semantic, and its nativity is the gap mult.seam-signature.

Notes

The collapse the decree blocks, using only laws of rungs ≤ Q. Start from o; by the unit law right to left, o ≐ ([o] [o]); by the product of negatives right to left, ≐ ([<o>] [<o>]). Abstract both sides: void ≐ [o] ≐ [([<o>] [<o>])], and one unguarded unit step, [([<o>][<o>])] → [<o>] [<o>], gives [<o>] [<o>] ≐ void — James's J-cancellation J J ≐ void, whose content is 2πi. From it: J ≐ <J> by Inversion; with H = ([J] <[oo]>) (half of J), cardinality gives H H ≐ J, and the ℚ sign rule for a mirrored numerator turns H ≐ ([H H] <[oo]>) ≐ ([<H H>] <[oo]>) into <H>; so J ≐ H H ≐ H <H> ≐ void, <o> ≐ ([<o>]) ≐ (void) ≐ o, and oo ≐ o <o> ≐ void. Every step but the marked one is exact in ℂ. The marked step is refused by this decree: its content has imaginary part 2π and its position (depth 0) is not absorbing. (An earlier Refuted entry spoke of "the collapse above"; it is this one.) Run backwards — [<o>] [<o>] → [([<o>] [<o>])] → [([o] [o])] → [o] → void — the same collapse uses the unit in the other orientation, which is why both are guarded. The same route runs, mutatis mutandis, from N = [[oo]], a negative number reached with no mirror: ([N][N]) ≐ ([<N>][<N>]) (both 0.1343), the unguarded step [([N][N])] → [N][N] (content −2.007 + 2πi), and J′ = [N] <[<N>]> (value iπ) in J's role — which is why the guard must look at values and not at mirrors (mult.seam-signature). The "ℚ sign rule for a mirrored numerator" above is Q.negative-fraction.

Price. The guard imports the ℂ reading, which overcharges: only Im X — the branch index — is needed, not the whole value (and not Im X mod 2π, which destroys exactly the information the strip test uses); a cheaper branch-reading import would price the sign laws more exactly. Laws whose unit steps are admitted by content at non-absorbing positions (alg.log-law and C.log-of-negative at depth 0; alg.root-of-product and alg.power-of-power under a square), and laws whose unit steps are seam steps admitted by position (Q.reciprocal-of-negative, C.period-absorption, C.euler-formula), declare guarded_by: [mult.seam-decree] — a field the checker computes from the derivation and enforces both ways — and so carry the guard in their price; their descendants inherit it through uses. Their status stays NATIVE: the decree adjudicates the step, it does not make the law true (Amendment A2, after the C referee pass found the two clauses priced inconsistently between rungs Q and C).

The engine enforces this decree directly (tools/check.py, check_seam): for every step that is a unit step, it evaluates the content on the node's sampled domain and refuses the step if the content leaves the strip in any sample while the position is not absorbing. Schemas are checked on their sampled instances; a law whose derivation needs an unguarded unit step for some instances must either restructure the step into an absorbing position or restrict its domain and say so.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That James's "crack" is deeper than the phase element: it is the absence, in an equational calculus of forms, of any term for the branch of a logarithm. The classical calculus is consistent only relative to a guard it imports. This is exactly the place where the enrichment program enters: 𝕁₁ does not guard the unit, it weakens it to [(A)] ≐ A mod Λ and records that the discrepancy lies in Λ as a receipt. A receipt is bookkeeping of an unknown, not detection — the calculus never determines which λ without the reading — but it dissolves the gap wherever an instance encloses the step (A5′ absorbs every λ) and leaves it open exactly for bare abstracts, which is what the J1 cells of alg.log-law and alg.power-of-power say. Seen from below, the receipt calculus is what this gap becomes.

Notes

LEGISLATION 27 scheduled this gap to close at rung J1. It closed there in two of its three positions (2026-10-04, J1.seam-theorem): inside an instance and at depth 0 the strip test became a receipt, and no import is needed. Under a square it did not close — ≃ is not a congruence through [ ] — and the ℂ import stands for exactly those steps, no longer provisional but located: the by-content guards of alg.power-of-base, alg.power-of-power, alg.root-of-product, alg.root-of-quotient, alg.sqrt4, C.i-to-the-i, C.root-of-negative, C.modulus-of-polar. The witness that no syntactic signature exists ([[[oo]]]) is now also the third door of J1.regime-split.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

Two cautions the argument needs. The guard covers the unit in both orientations ([(X)] ≐ X is false off the strip either way). And the admissible calculus is not substitution-closed: a derived schema such as alg.log-law is admissible only on the domain where its own derivation is — instantiated at A = B = <o> it is the collapse step — so a law may be cited only inside its declared domain; the engine re-evaluates every row, which is how it catches a bad instantiation.

James's soundness result, scoped exactly: the calculus is consistent as a calculus of admissible derivations under the J-discipline, and both devices are hinges, not afterthoughts. Once the unit is guarded, soundness is immediate — every other rule is an identity of complex arithmetic — so the whole weight of consistency rests on a guard the calculus cannot state in its own terms. It is not yet re-established for the enriched settings, each of which changes the reading and the axioms (JH-22 is the JH version: consistency relative to ℍ).

Refuted readings

  • the unrestricted equational theory of the pilot's laws is consistent — refuted 2026-10-03 (first referee pass). Route A: with [□] admitted, W = (o [□]) satisfies W ≐ W (o [C]) by Dominion-under-square and Distribution, so Inversion gives (o [C]) ≐ void for every C, hence o ≐ void.
  • Route B needs rung C (a named J) — refuted the same day (second referee pass): J J = [<o>][<o>] is writable at rung mult; one unguarded unit step gives J J ≐ void, and the ℚ sign rules finish the collapse (recorded at mult.seam-decree). The first draft of this node deferred the guard to rung C; it is needed from rung mult on.

Notes

The engine enforces the undefined-form decree by exception and the seam decree as a rule (check_seam: every unit step's content is evaluated on the node's sampled domain and refused off the strip outside an absorbing position); near-real values are snapped onto the axis before a log so the branch cut is not decided by rounding. The witness tools/models/consistency_check.py is a property test of the lemmas — the exactness of the other rules on complex content, absorption in absorbing positions, non-vacuity of the decree, separation of piles — not a proof; the engine tier here means that much and no more. Its first run refuted the syntactic signature ([[[oo]]]), which is how mult.seam-signature came to exist.

(−a)⁻¹ = −a⁻¹, by uniqueness of inverses, as in any field. What the chart adds is the price: three of the steps are the unit on content off the principal strip, admitted only because they sit inside an instance — seam steps, so the law declares guarded_by (by position) and is the first sign law to carry the decree in its price (its status stays NATIVE: the decree adjudicates the steps, it does not make the law true — Amendment A2). In J1 the same three steps post receipts of ±2πi, and the law holds exactly by the depth-1 criterion; these are the first ℚ laws whose receipts do not vanish. The engine passes every row because it evaluates whole rows: the periods cancel inside the instance.

([A] <[B]>) ≐ ([C] <[D]>) iff ([A] [D]) ≐ ([C] [B])
a/b = c/d ⟺ ad = cb

Two fractions are the same number exactly when top-times-other-bottom matches on both sides — the page can run either direction, but "exactly when" is a sentence about the page, not a form on it.

Multiply both sides by ([B] [D]): on the left, ([([A]<[B]>)] [([B][D])]) ≐ ([A] <[B]> [B] [D]) ≐ ([A] [D]) — two unit steps and one Inversion; on the right, likewise ([C] <[D]> [B] [D]) ≐ ([C] [B])mult.multiplication mult.involution Z.inversioncongruence: equals multiplied by equals are equal; the unit steps are on real content

The chart keeps it meta because its content is an iff; each direction's instances are engine-checkable, and the object-level laws it leans on are. It is not a canonical form: it decides equality without choosing a representative.

The base

e:=
e := (o)e = e^1 = 2.71828…

A circle around a circle is the number e — the first number on the page that no fraction can name.

classical holdsJ1 holdsJH holdsJO holdsJP replacedC EXACTfinset PARTIALlambda untestedCC untestedlogic ABSENT

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

e as e^1, the value the exponential takes at the unit. What this does not do is constrain the base: the three axioms never mention a value for (o) — read with (A) = b^A and [A] = log_b A, every object-level law of the chart holds for any base b > 0, b ≠ 1 (checked for b = 2, 10, ½ by the alg referee pass), so the calculus cannot even refute e ≐ oo: in the base-2 reading (o) and oo have the same value. Where the classical setting does commit to e is the ℂ reading it imports (mult.c-reading, (A) = e^A) and the seam decree that inherits it, whose strip (−π, π] is base e's. Whether the rules determine every true identity of exp and log is a different question, the exp–log completeness question of the analysis rung. Transcendence of e (Hermite 1873) is an import the calculus cannot state (alg.irrationality is the simpler version of the same gap).

James, p. 47 and p. 50: "The base of these operations is not constrained by the calculus … An equality could be introduced that defined this to be non-transcendental, such as base two with the definition (o) ≐ oo. Everything in the calculus would still hold as none of it is dependent on this value." — the chart's base finding, in his words; (o) is his e (p. 48, glossary p. 63), "incommensurable with any other boundary construction".

The census's size-3 constants (<o>) (1/e) and <(o)> (−e) are the chart's smallest illustration of the JH Depth Principle: the same two boundaries, nested the other way, name different numbers. Both are assigned to this node; (o) o likewise.

Refuted readings

  • Lehmer's number is a radical form — refuted 2026-10-01 in the exp–log thread: the Galois group of its degree-5 trace polynomial is S₅, so the Galois group of the degree-10 Lehmer polynomial is not solvable. (The first record here said "is a form" and "Galois group S₅" of the Lehmer polynomial itself; both corrected 2026-10-03 — the group of the degree-10 polynomial lies in C₂ ≀ S₅ and is larger than S₅.)
  • the real root of x⁵ − x − 1 is not ≐ any form — overclaimed 2026-10-03 and corrected the same day: Abel–Ruffini excludes radical forms only; the exp–log case is Chow's conjecture.

Notes

x⁵ − x − 1 is the standard example: irreducible over ℚ, discriminant 2869 = 19·151, Galois group S₅, one real root. Chow, "What is a closed-form number?", Amer. Math. Monthly 106 (1999).

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

ln(−e^a) = a + iπ for real a — the principal branch's rule for the exponential of a negated exponential — and James's observation that the phase operator is "independent of its contents". What it is not: a law for every form A, as James states it (p. 44). At A = J the left side is [<(J)>] = [<<o>>] = [o], which is void, and the right side is J J, which is 2πi; James's Theorem 2, "J Cancellation" J J ≐ void (p. 45), is exactly this theorem at A = J, run right to left — and it is from Theorem 2 that the ambiguous sign and cardinality of J follow (§6.3). So the crack in the calculus is one row long and has an address: the last line of the proof above, taken on content off the strip. Everything else in James's proof is exact. The chart's C.log-of-negative ([<A>] ≐ [A] J, James's rule 1) and C.phase-under-instance (<(A)> ≐ (A J)) are the two "concise forms of inverse promotion" he derives from this theorem on p. 45; the second is exact for every A because its unit step sits inside an instance.

Confirms

The period of exp: e^{a + 2πi} = e^a for every complex a. This is the sound content of James's "J-cancellation": the pair cancels inside an instance because the instance forgets whole turns, and the derivation says exactly where that happens — the unit step is taken in the absorbing position, which the seam decree admits unconditionally. Its content 2πi is off the strip, so the step is a seam step and the law carries the decree in its price (guarded_by, by position): a law whose statement is an exact identity of ℂ while its derivation leans on the decree, as Q.reciprocal-of-negative and C.phase-under-instance before it. It is not J J ≐ void, and it is not [A J J] ≐ [A]: under a square J J is just the summand 2πi, and ln(a + 2πi) is not ln a. In J1 this law is the completion axiom A5′ itself, (λ A) ≐ (A) for λ ∈ Λ, at λ = ω.

Confirms

1 + ω + ω² = 0, proved as the textbook proves it — (ω − 1)(ω² + ω + 1) = ω³ − 1 = 0 and ω ≠ 1 — but with the division made explicit: the sum S is multiplied by (ω − 1)/(ω − 1), which is o by Q.self-division, the product collapses to nothing by ω³ ≐ o (C.cube-root-of-unity) and three Inversions, and (□ <[ω − 1]>) is void by the hole rules. The forms do not need "no zero divisors": what carries that weight is the invertibility of ω − 1 — a reading-level fact, ω ≠ 1, of the same kind as alg.irrationality — together with (□ C) ≐ void. The same cancellation for the n-th roots of unity, every n, is schema.roots-sum. It is not a proof that ω is irrational or that it generates a field of degree 2: those are statements about which other forms equal ω, i.e. about the reading, like alg.irrationality.

ℂ = ℝ + ℝi, the rectangular form, with the arithmetic of complex numbers being the arithmetic of forms — addition is juxtaposition, multiplication is ([X][Y]), and the laws of the earlier rungs apply unchanged. What the page does not do is make the spelling canonical: the same number has many forms (the polar spelling C.polar-form is another), and "two complex numbers are equal iff their parts are" is a statement about the ℂ reading (mult.consistency), not a law of the forms. The forms do not know that they are pairs.

The polar form r e^{iθ} with θ = πt. Multiplication of complex numbers in polar form is the addition of logs and of counts — ([R₁] ([J][T₁])) × ([R₂] ([J][T₂])) collects under one instance by the exponential law — and division is the mirror. The angle-addition formulas of trigonometry follow from these two moves applied to the cosine and sine forms (C.turn-of-sum, C.cosine-addition, C.sine-addition); the product with moduli is C.polar-product. It is not canonical: t and t + 2 give the same value by C.period-absorption, and the form does not reduce one to the other; a principal t ∈ (−1, 1] is a choice made in the reading.

Confirms

Euler's cos θ = (e^{iθ} + e^{−iθ})/2 taken as the definition, with θ = πt — the order of exposition of a complex-analysis course, not of a geometry one. The angle is in half-turns because the count is of J. It is not a geometric definition and does not need one: the right triangle enters the chart, if at all, at the rung analysis where lengths are. The form has 23 boundaries.

Confirms

The rectangular formula for a quotient. What the derivation shows is that division needs nothing new: ([z] <[w]>) was a form at rung Q for any nonzero w, and the "realize the denominator" trick is one Inversion, one Collection, and the modulus identity. It is not a definition of division in ℂ — division was defined once, at Q.division, for all forms — and it is not needed to compute with the chart's forms; it is needed to read them in the way the textbook does.

The seam steps the engine finds are the units on [([B] [i])] and [([D] [i])] (content ln b + iπ/2, which is ln|b| + 3πi/2 for negative b) and the right-to-left units on the real products [A] [C], [A] [D], [B] [C], [B] [D] (content 2πi + ln|ac| when both factors are negative); all sit directly inside instances. The unit right to left on [w] [w̄] is free on the sampled domain: the two arguments cancel for every d ≠ 0, and d = 0 — where the content would be 2 ln|w| + 2πi for c < 0 — is not in the domain, since [D] would be the hole. For the same reason 1/(c + di) is not an instance of this law (b = 0 is the hole): the reciprocal is (<[w]>) directly, and its rectangular form follows by the same rows with z = o.

Confirms

Euler's sin θ = (e^{iθ} − e^{−iθ})/2i as the definition. Together with C.cosine this gives trigonometry its two functions with no geometry spent; that they reassemble the turn is C.euler-formula. The form has 36 boundaries, the largest named form in the chart so far (the sides of the cube-root laws are larger) — a reminder that the calculus is an assembly language for ℂ, in which the standard names are abbreviations worth having. What sine is not, here: a ratio of lengths, or anything periodic by definition — its period is inherited from C.period-absorption through the phase.

C.euler-formulatheoremNATIVEengineshape-ledband 9–12○

Euler's formula — the turn is cosine plus i sine

≐

A turn is "how far along" plus i times "how far up". Having defined the two parts by splitting the turn, the law checks that the split loses nothing.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ, with θ = πt, as a theorem of the three axioms — every step exact as a row, every unit step in an absorbing position, so the law holds for every t; the first unit step is a seam step (the sine's interior is off the strip when the sine is negative), so the derivation leans on the decree's position clause and the law carries it in its price. What the derivation is: the algebra (X + 1/X)/2 + i·(X − 1/X)/(2i) = X, done in forms. What it is not: Euler's own route, which defines cos and sin by their series and proves the formula analytically — the chart has no series until rung analysis, so here cos and sin were defined from the exponential, and the formula records that the definitions are the right ones. The Pythagorean identity cos² + sin² = 1 is the natural companion, C.pythagorean — the product X · 1/X = 1 in disguise. At t = 1 the sine vanishes into the hole and the law reads (J) ≐ <o>, which is C.phase-value; C.euler-identity is one Inversion further.

Notes

The left side has 7 boundaries and the right 72: the standard notation's economy is bought with the names cos, sin and i, each of which is a sizeable form. The chart's view is that the names are worth having and the forms are worth having once.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

cos θ − i sin θ = e^{−iθ}: Euler's formula at −θ, with the evenness of cosine and oddness of sine carrying the sign. This is the theorem that lets the conjugate of a number be read off either spelling; with C.modulus-squared it gives z z̄ = r² for the polar form, since ([turn] [reverse turn]) is o by C.turn-of-sum. It is not a new definition of the conjugate — there is none for a general form — but the agreement of the two the chart has.

cos² + sin² = 1 from the exponential definitions: (X + X̄)²/4 − (X − X̄)²/4 = X X̄ = 1. Twenty-one rows, because the page expands the squares by hand; but the content is one fact, ([X] [(<[X]>)]) ≐ o, which is the reciprocal law. It is not the theorem of Pythagoras about triangles — no lengths, no right angle — but the identity that will become it when the rung analysis reads lengths into moduli; and it is not a definition of the circle, which the page does not have.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

r e^{iθ}= r, for positive r: r²(cos² + sin²) = r², and √(r²) = r. The last step is the one that costs: √(r²) ≐ r goes through the log law under a square — a unit step nothing absorbs, admitted because 2 ln r is real — so the law is guarded by content — the same step as alg.log-law, taken here on [R] [R] — and would be false for negative r (√(r²) =r). It is not the triangle inequality or any other metric fact: those wait for the rung analysis.

Notes

Guarded by content and by position (Amendment A2). By content: the log-law step [([R] [R])] → [R] [R] sits under a square, where nothing absorbs, and is admitted because its content 2 ln r is real. By position: the right-to-left units on [cos πT] [cos πT] and [sin πT] [sin πT] in the second table have content 2 Ln(cos πt), resp. 2 Ln(sin πt), which is 2 ln|cos πt| + 2πi whenever the cosine is negative (t = 0.75: −0.693 + 6.283i) — off the strip — and sit directly inside an instance; so does the unit on the turn in the bridge for |t| > 1. The units on [([R] [cos πT])] themselves are free: their content ln r + Ln(cos πt) has imaginary part 0 or π, on the strip. The law carries the decree in its price on both counts.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

cos(s+t) = cos s cos t − sin s sin t, with the usual exponential proof made into rows. The whole formula is a shadow of C.turn-of-sum: XY is the turn of s + t and X̄Ȳ its reverse, and the cosine is half their sum. It is not proved for angles given geometrically — s and t are counts of J. The engine samples real counts; the same rows are exact for complex counts too (the cosine form is then the complex cosine, which is cosh along the imaginary axis), so the restriction is one of sampling, not of the law.

With C.pythagorean, the longest derivation on the chart so far (21 rows); the engine checks every row on sampled real s, t, including the rows with eight summands.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

sin(s+t) = sin s cos t + cos s sin t. Compared with the cosine formula, the i² step is not needed: there is one <[i]> in each product and it is carried through unchanged. It is not the only route — the formula is also the imaginary part of C.turn-of-sum expanded by Euler's formula — but that route needs "imaginary part", which is a reading, not a form; this one stays on the page.

De Moivre — the cube of a turn is the turn tripled

≐
(([[(([J] [T]))]] [ooo])) ≐ (([J] [T] [ooo]))(([o o o] [[(([T] [J]))]])) ≐ (([o o o] [T] [J]))(e^{iπt})³ = e^{3iπt}

Cube a turn and you have turned three times as far. The page proves it by turning the cube into a triple product and adding up the three counts.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

(cos θ + i sin θ)^n = cos nθ + i sin nθ, at n = 3 and for every real θ — with no principal-branch condition, because the power is unfolded into a product before any log is taken: the only unit steps are inside the instance. It is not the general law: for a general numeral n the unfolding (([[X]] [n])) ≐ ([X] … [X]) and the cardinality of n copies are schemas over n — schema.power and schema.cardinality, and De Moivre for every n is schema.de-moivre, all priced with the induction gap (N.induction); this node is the instance n = 3 the reader meets first. And it is not true for a non-numeral exponent without a condition: (([[X]] [N])) with N a real count is X^N in the principal sense, e^{N·Ln X}, which equals the turn by Nt exactly when N(t − τ) is an even integer, τ being t reduced into (−1, 1] — always for integer N (which is De Moivre), and for every N when t is already in (−1, 1].

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The quadratic formula as a factorization identity, exact for every complex x and every a ≠ 0 — expanded here from the factored side, the way one checks the formula, which is the reverse of James's completing-the-square derivation (pp. 76–79: introduce 1/a from the void, work d and e in, flatten, complete the square, make a difference of squares, separate the factors). Where the textbook writes ±, the page writes f and <f>, two forms the calculus keeps apart; the two "solutions" are the equation ([A] [X d f] [X d <f>]) ≐ void read with Q.no-division-by-zero's companion — a product is void only if a factor is — which is a reading-level fact, not a law of the forms. It is not an algorithm for roots (James: "an informed calculation", p. 75) and not restricted to a positive discriminant: for d² − e < 0 the form f is a quarter-turn times a real root (C.root-of-negative), and the identity holds unchanged.

C.james-disciplinetheoremNATIVE-BY-DECREEenginemetaneed-ledband beyond○

James's J-discipline sits inside the seam decree

James's two J-rules, as the chart records them — convert [<A>] to [A] J on sight; cancel J J only inside an instance, and last — sit inside the seam decree: rule 1 is admitted exactly on content with Im Ln A ∈ (−π, 0] and refuted elsewhere, rule 2 is period absorption, and the decree is strictly stronger than both, since it adjudicates every unit step and not only those through J
ln(−a) = ln a + iπ only for Im Ln a ∈ (−π, 0]; e^{z + 2πi} = e^z always; 2πi ≠ 0; the Involution route to J J = 0 is closed by neither J-rule

James patched the crack by giving rules for handling J. The chart patched it by giving a rule for undoing a circle with a box. The chart's patch covers James's and more — and James's first rule, taken literally, is itself cracked.

classical holdsJ1 replacedJH replacedJO replacedJP untestedC EXACTfinset ABSENTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic ABSENT
Derivation

The J-rules compared here are James's two constraints of Ch. 6 §6.3, p. 47, quoted: (1) "Convert inverse boundaries to Js. Whenever the inverse boundary is wrapped by the abstract boundary, as [<A>], pull the inverse out, as [A] J." (2) "Limit J cancellation. Allow Js to cancel only within an instance boundary and after applying other reductions." The thesis is in the repository (references/james-1993-calculus-of-number.pdf).

statementrulenote
Rule 1 ⊂ content clause, restricted. "Convert [<A>] to [A] J on sight" is the law C.log-of-negative, whose one step is the unit at depth 0 on content [A] J. The decree admits it exactly when Im Ln A ∈ (−π, 0] — positive A and the lower half-plane — and the equation is false by 2πi otherwise, so James's rule as stated is unsound: it fails at A = <o> and at A = [[oo]], a negative real with no mirror in sight. The chart's rule 1 is the restriction to positive A, with C.log-of-negative-below as its companion on the other sideC.log-of-negative C.log-of-negative-below mult.seam-decreewitness part (1): on wide complex sampling the conversion is exact in roughly half the samples and off by exactly 2πi in the rest, with the boundary predicted by the strip test in every sample
Rule 2 ⊂ position clause. "Cancel J J only inside an instance, and last" is C.period-absorption (A J J) ≐ (A): the unit step it hides is a seam step taken in an absorbing position, which the decree admits; the ordering clause is unnecessary once admissibility is decided by positionC.period-absorption C.double-phasewitness part (2): exact on 300 complex samples
The decree is strictly stronger. (a) It adjudicates unit steps that involve no J at all: the seam steps of Q.reciprocal-of-negative have content −ln a − iπ and 2πi, and the J-rules say nothing about them. (b) The collapse route of mult.seam-decree reaches J J ≐ void not by cancelling J J but by one Involution step [(J J)] → J J at depth 0 — a step neither J-rule, as paraphrased, forbids; the decree refuses it by content, in both orientationsmult.seam-decree Q.reciprocal-of-negativewitness part (3): the engine's own seam check refuses [(J J)] ↔ J J both ways and admits the same step directly inside an instance, through an angle too
What the J-rules leave implicit — that J and <J> differ on the page and agree under an instance — is C.phase-signC.phase-signwitness part (4)
Where the two repairs differ in kind: James's rules are syntactic ("on sight", "inside an instance") and the first is unsound for that reason — the content [A] J leaves the strip for some A without any visible sign; the decree is semantic, and that it must be is the gap mult.seam-signaturemult.seam-signature—
Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That the classical setting of the chart — three boundaries, three axioms, two decrees — contains the classical James algebra of the thesis: three boundaries, three axioms, J, and the J-discipline. The discipline is not a fourth axiom and not a convention about J; it is a procedural shadow of the condition under which the unit step is harmless — true on the strip, absorbed inside an instance — and J is where the condition first bites: <J> (four boundaries, value −iπ) is the smallest form whose content leaves the half-open strip, and J J the smallest whose content leaves it by a whole period. What this node does not show: that the two repairs are equivalent (they are not — the decree is strictly stronger, and rule 1 is refuted as stated); that the decree is the only repair (J1 prices the step with a receipt instead of refusing it, and JH guards one orientation semantically); or that the decree follows from the axioms (it is adjoined, in both tellings). The text has now been checked against the thesis: James's constraints are exactly the two quoted above (p. 47); he does not restrict Involution-down, and his own proof of phase independence (p. 44) takes the unguarded unit step at depth 0 as its last line — which is where the crack is, in the chart's reading (C.phase-independence).

Refuted readings

  • the J-discipline and the seam decree are the same rule — the first statement of this node (2026-10-03, same day); refuted by its own body in the C referee pass: the decree adjudicates non-J seam steps and the Involution route to the crack, which the J-rules do not, and rule 1 as stated is false off the lower half-plane. Struck, and the node restated as an inclusion.
  • the J-discipline is a convention about a special symbol J, separate from the axioms — it is a special case of the admissibility condition on the unit step of mult.involution, which the chart states before J is named (an interpretive thesis, recorded rather than witnessed).

The refutations of J J ≐ void and J ≐ <J> as depth-0 laws, and of the on-sight rule for every A, live at C.double-phase, C.phase-sign and C.log-of-negative respectively.

Notes

The witness tools/models/j_discipline.py tests four facts of the ℂ reading and one behaviour of the engine (check_seam, the chart's implementation of the decree); it witnesses the rows above, not a theorem about two derivation systems — that would need James's rules formalized from the text. Citations are to J. M. James, A Calculus of Number Based on Spatial Forms, M.S. thesis, University of Washington, 1993 — Ch. 6 "Phase", pp. 43–50; the thesis is in references/. The 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-03 sessions found the collapse route independently and legislated the decree at rung mult under referee pressure; this node closes that loop by placing James's own rules inside it.

Confirms

James's cardinality theorem (p. 27): "Multiple references in the same context may be reduced to a single reference with multiple units signifying its quantity, as A…A = ([A][o…o])" — his base A = ([A]) = ([A][o]) is the base table (one row, since the chart's mult.unit-law is already ([A][o]) ≐ A), and his step A…AA = ([A][o…o])([A][o]) = ([A][o…oo]) is the step table. mult.cardinality, the chart's n = 2, is the first derived instance. The engine checks the base at n = 1, the step at every n from 2 to 12, and that the hypothesis row is this law at n − 1; what it does not check is the passage to all n — that is N.induction, cited in the hypothesis row, and the reason the status is NATIVE-BY-SCHEMA rather than NATIVE. Everything in rung C that was written out for n = 2 or 3 by hand (C.i-squared, C.cube-root-of-unity, C.de-moivre) is an instance of what this rung states once.

Confirms

x ⋯ x = xⁿ as James states it (p. 28: ([x]…[x]) = (([[x]][o…o]))), proved by induction on n: the count n is the count n − 1 beside a unit, Distribution splits the two, the hypothesis handles the n − 1, and one absorbing unit step puts the last factor in. It is not valid for a non-numeral exponent — (([[A]] [B])) with B a general form is the exponential, and "B factors" means nothing — and it is not restricted to positive a: every unit step sits inside an instance, so the schema is exact on ℂ× (guarded by position for complex a, where (n − 1) ln a leaves the strip).

e^{a + 2πin} = e^a for every n ≥ 1 (the negative multiples need one Inversion more, <J J> beside J J, and are not stated here): the kernel of the exponential is all of 2πiℤ, not just its generator — which in J1 is A5′ for the whole lattice Λ = ℤω (the chart's (λ A) ≐ (A)). James's "ambiguous cardinality" void = JJ = JJJJ = … (p. 46) is exactly this schema with the instance removed, which is the crack; with the instance kept it is a theorem. It is not a statement about odd counts of J: an odd number of J inside an instance is a sign (C.phase-under-instance, schema.roots-of-negation).

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The n-th roots of unity as James gestured at them (p. 46) and as the chart can now state them: (([J] [2k] <[n]>)) for k = 1, …, n, each satisfying ωⁿ = 1. Their multiplication is the addition of counts, and schema.period-multiple reduces the count modulo 2 — so they form the cyclic group ℤ/n, with k = n the identity o. What this schema is not: a proof that these are all the n-th roots of unity, or that they are distinct — the first needs that a polynomial of degree n has at most n roots, which is a statement about the reading, and the second needs an order or a count of forms up to ≐, which the chart does not have (N.order). It also is not yet the cyclotomic relation that they sum to nothing; that is schema.roots-sum.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The n-th roots of −1 as fractional counts of J: (([J] [2k+1] <[n]>)) for k = 0, …, n − 1. The derivation differs from schema.roots-of-unity in one row: the odd J left over after the whole turns are forgotten becomes a sign by C.phase-under-instance. Together the two schemas say that μ_{2n} = μ_n ⊔ (the roots of negation) — the unity/negation split that J1 reads as group and torsor. It does not say which of the n forms is real: for odd n the count 1 (k = (n − 1)/2) gives (J), which is <o> itself, the real n-th root of −1 — but "real" is a question for the reading, like alg.irrationality.

De Moivre's formula, for every n

≐
(([[(([J] [T]))]] [o^{n}])) ≐ (([J] [T] [o^{n}]))(e^{iπt})ⁿ = e^{iπnt}
drawn at n = 3; checked for n=1..6

Turn by t, n times over: you have turned by nt. The page unfolds the power into n turns and adds the counts.

classical holdsJ1 holdsJH guardedJO guardedJP guardedC EXACTfinset ABSENTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic ABSENT

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

De Moivre's formula as a schema over n, with no principal-branch condition on t: the power is unfolded into a product by schema.power before any abstract of the turn is taken, so the only unit steps sit inside the instance. It is not true for a non-numeral exponent without a condition (see C.de-moivre, Confirms), and it is not the formula with cosines and sines on the page — that spelling needs C.euler-formula on both sides, which is a further row the chart leaves to the reader.

≐void
Σ{j=1..n: (([J] [o^{2j}] <[o^{n}]>))} ≐ voidω + ω² + … + ωⁿ = 0 (n ≥ 2)

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

Σ ω^j = 0 for n ≥ 2, the sum of all n-th roots of unity, proved by telescoping: (ω − 1)·Σ_{j=1}^{n} ω^j = ω^{n+1} − ω = 0 since ω^{n+1} = ω by a whole turn (C.period-absorption), and dividing nothing by ω − 1 ≠ 0 is nothing. That ω − 1 is not void for n ≥ 2 — ω ≠ 1 — is a fact about the reading, of the same kind as alg.irrationality: the calculus cannot derive it, Q.self-division needs it, and the schema is exactly as good as it. (At n = 1 the "sum" is o and the law is false, which is why the range starts at 2.) The rows with Σ are templates: "Distribution n − 1 times", "Inversion, n − 1 pairs"; the engine instantiates them for n = 2 … 6 and checks each. It is not a statement about the proper n-th roots alone (the primitive ones sum to the Möbius value μ(n)), and it is not Gauss's theory of periods — only its first identity. Every row has the value 0, so, as for C.omega-sum, the engine certifies 0 = 0 and the seam check; the licensing is the referee's.

The period form ω

:=
ω := [()]ω = 2πi, the period of the exponential; Λ = ℤω

Walk once around the circle and you are back where you started — but 𝕁₁ remembers that you walked. ω is the form that remembers.

Derivation

ω		namethe period form
Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

ω = 2πi as the generator of the period lattice of exp: e^{ω} = 1 and no smaller nonzero multiple of it has that property. The hinge of the whole enriched program: ln 1 has every branch 2πik, and the classical calculus chose k = 0 by erasing [()]; 𝕁₁ chooses to name the branch instead. It is not a new axiom: no equation is adjoined here; a strict rule has been withdrawn, which is why ω is irreducible by strict rules. It is not the half-period: J = [<()>] = iπ is the log of −1, half of ω (J1.half-period), and the two differ as a group differs from its torsor — unity has an identity, negation has none.

Notes

The reading convention is a choice of lift: any 2πik with k ≠ 0 would do as the value of ω, and k = 1 is the generator. The reading is compositional (LEGISLATION 30b as amended): the log of exactly one — [()], [(ω)], [(J J)] alike — is 2πi, every other log principal; the engine uses it for nodes in setting: J1 and for every receipt on every card, while the trunk's own numeric checks keep ln 1 = 0. That is why mult.log-of-one's 𝕁₁ tape shows the receipt ω, and why [(J J)] → J J shows none.

The counit is strict

none — adjoined: the first axiom of 𝕁₁, which is the first axiom of the classical calculus read in one direction, stated in terms of the two boundaries N.round and mult.square. Its classical shadow is the counit row of mult.involution (see also); every counit step on the trunk is strict in 𝕁₁ (receipt prover: census/j1-ledger.md).

Confirms

exp ∘ ln = id on ℂ× unconditionally — the asymmetry of the two halves of Involution is the asymmetry of exp and ln: exp is single-valued, ln is not. In the adjunction reading, ( ) ⊣ [ ] is a reflective localization and this is the strict counit of a fully faithful right adjoint. It is not the unit [(A)] ≡ A, which fails by a lattice element: [(J J J)] is iπ, J J J is 3iπ.

J1.unitaxiomNATIVEengineneed-ledband beyond○

The unit is witnessed

≃
[(A)] ≃ Aln e^a = a mod 2πi — with the receipt [e^a] − a ∈ Λ, void exactly on the strip −π < Im a ≤ π, off the lattice itself: at a = mω the instance is exactly one, the log reads ω, and the receipt is (1 − m)ω — ω at a = 0, void at a = ω

Box a circle and you get back what you circled — except that going round the circle may have added a whole turn, and 𝕁₁ writes that turn on a receipt instead of pretending it did not happen.

classical replacedJ1 holdsJH guardedJO guardedJP holdsC EXACTfinset untestedlambda untestedCC untestedlogic untested
Derivation

none — adjoined, in terms of the two boundaries N.round and mult.square: the unit half of mult.involution (see also), weakened. The receipt is not a form on the page: it is the name of the identification [(A)] ≃ A, a 2-cell in the two-cell presentation, and its value — a multiple of the period form J1.period-form — is read off by the reading. The engine's position rule for the receipt (SPEC §5.5): absorbed when the step is taken directly inside an instance (through angles at most) — the instance pays it, and the result is value-exact; posted at depth 0 — the two forms agree mod Λ; under a square the step is not taken at all, because ≃ does not pass through [ ] (the depth-one criterion, J1.seam-theorem).

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

ln ∘ exp = id mod 2πiℤ — the multivaluedness of the logarithm stated as an equation with a remainder rather than as a prohibition. James's two constraints of procedure (p. 47), the chart's seam decree, and this axiom are three responses to the same fact; this is the one that keeps the information. It is not a weakening of the calculus's power: every classical law still holds, strictly or with absorbed receipts or mod Λ (J1.classical-floor). It is not a statement about which branch is principal: the receipt names the difference between two logs, never a preferred one — the design rule "no absolute laws, only differences and exchanges" (𝕁 v3.1).

An instance absorbs a period

≃
(ω A) ≃ (A)(A ω) ≃ (A)e^{2πi + a} = e^a — the instance pays the receipt ω

Inside a circle a whole turn changes nothing — e^{a + 2πi} = e^a — and 𝕁₁ writes down that it swallowed a turn.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

e^{z + 2πi} = e^z: the kernel of exp is Λ, all of it. On the chart this is the law behind every "[o] ≐ void inside an instance" of the trunk — mult.log-of-one used in an absorbing position — and behind C.period-absorption (A J J) ≐ (A). In the July presentation A5′ had to be forced: with a unit weak only mod Λ and no receipts, the critical pair ([()][A]) reduces to A by one branch and to (ω [A]) by the other, and they join only if absorption holds. With receipts the pair is not critical — both branches are ≃-equal with tapes that cancel — and the law is a theorem. It is not strict: the tape is not empty, it is paid. Evaluation (≈, J1.classical-floor) forgets the payment; 𝕁₁ does not.

J1.linearitydecreeNATIVE-BY-DECREEhandmetaneed-ledband beyonddiscipline○

Receipts are linear

DISCIPLINE — the receipt context admits exchange only: a receipt is emitted by exactly one application of the unit (or of absorption) and consumed by exactly one; no receipt is duplicated (contraction) or discarded (weakening) within 𝕁₁
the tape is a multiset of ±ω tokens that is never contracted or weakened; forgetting it is the evaluation ≈

Every turn you take gets one ticket, and the ticket can be handed round but not torn up or photocopied. Tear them all up and you are back in James's calculus; photocopy them and the arithmetic of the wall is gone.

classical replacedJ1 holdsJH untestedJO untestedJP untestedC EXACTfinset untestedlambda untestedCC untestedlogic EXACT
Derivation
statementrulenote
Weakening = absorption = the classical floor. Allow a receipt to be dropped anywhere, and [(A)] ≃ A becomes [(A)] ≐ A: James's strict unit, with its crack (J1.unit, C.phase-independence). Allowing it only inside instances is J1.absorption, which is not weakening — the instance paysJ1.unit J1.absorptionT-L1: 𝕁₀ = 𝕁₁ + weakening + contraction on the receipt context; evaluation ≈ is defined as adjoining the structural rules (J1.classical-floor)
Contraction collapses Λ. Allow two receipts ω, ω to merge into one, and 2ω ~ ω; in ℤω that forces ω ~ 0 — the grading is gone, as surely as by weakening, only by the other structural rule — and with it every fraction of ω and the selection rule of the ψ-wall (J1.psi-wall)J1.period-form𝕁 v3.1: "contraction on receipts = collapse of the grading Λ = ℤω → destroys ω/24, the wall, the arithmetic"
What the engine's tape enforces of L0. No weakening: a posted receipt is never dropped — it makes the law ≃ (holds-mod-Λ), and a theorem whose receipts were absorbed is reused as a witnessed move, never promoted to ≡. No contraction within a derivation: each unit step is its own entry with its own content and receipt. What it does not represent: exchange (the tape is a multiset), the merging of duplicate entries across a schema's instances, and a reused theorem's tape beyond its grade (SPEC §5.5)—tools/j1.py; the ledger census/j1-ledger.md
Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The polarized-linear-logic dictionary of 𝕁 v3.1: ( ) and collection as positive and negative connectives, the receipt tape as a Geometry-of-Interaction execution trace, L0 as the linearity of the context, and 𝕁₀ = 𝕁₁ + (W, C) as classical = linear + structural rules. It is not a rule of the page: no form is affected; it is a rule about proofs. And it is not yet enforced for exchange in any interesting sense by the engine, whose tape is a multiset (exchange is free); what the engine enforces is the absence of weakening and of contraction within a derivation, as the row above says.

Ln(−1) = iπ + 2πiℤ: the multivaluedness of the logarithm, stated for the one value the calculus names. James's two constraints of procedure (p. 47; C.james-discipline) were written to keep this ambiguity from being used; 𝕁₁ uses it. It is not J ≐ <J> (James's other symptom, C.phase-sign): J <J> is void strictly by Inversion and J J is ω, so J and <J> differ by ω on the page — J ≃ <J> mod Λ, exactly as James saw, and not strictly. The coset structure: Λ = ℤω ⊂ ½Λ = ℤJ, with ½Λ/Λ = ℤ/2 = {unity, negation} — the group and the torsor.

J1.regime-splittheoremNATIVEenginemetaneed-ledband beyond○

Where the lattice enters

a form built from ( ), [ ], positive variables and piles, with no angle, no count of one ([()] = ω) and no square directly inside a square, has a void receipt at every unit step at every generic point; each of the three — an angle, a count of one, a square in a square — admits the lattice, and at the exceptional points — a square whose content is exactly one: a variable at one, AB = 1, B + C = 1 — the count of one enters by value
ℝ₊ is Λ-free: logs of sums of positive reals are real; the lattice enters through −1 (the angle), through ln 1 = ω (the count of one), and through ln ln a for a < 1 (nested squares)

Add, multiply and take roots of positive numbers and you never need a receipt. Three things open the door to the lattice: a minus sign, the log of one, and taking the log of a log.

Confirms

The local/colocal split of the July set, made exact: the Λ-free sector is not "angle-free" but "angle-free, ω-free and without nested squares" — James's canonical numeral forms, products and roots of positives — at generic points; the exceptional points, where a content is exactly one, are the receptacle's (J1.receptacle) and belong to the colocal side whatever the form says. It is not a statement about values alone: [[[oo]]] has a positive real under every square and still reaches the lattice, because a log of a positive real can be negative. And it is not the ψ-wall: which fractions of ω survive is a further selection (J1.psi-wall); this only says where fractions of ω can arise.

Confirms

ζₙ = e^{2πi/n} satisfies ζₙⁿ = 1, for every n in the range. Beside schema.roots-of-unity it says that the two routes to the roots of unity — fractions of J and fractions of ω — agree, as they must, since 2J ≃ ω. It is not the statement that these are all the n-th roots of unity, nor that they are distinct (both need an order or a count of forms, N.order); and it is not yet the selection of which ω/n are well formed at a given level — that is the ψ-wall, J1.psi-wall, the first place the chart's arithmetic becomes the arithmetic of the sphere.

Confirms

Ln(−e^a) ≡ a + iπ (mod 2πi) for every complex a — the statement that is actually true, with the actual remainder. The classical chart located the crack in this row (its content is 2πi at A = J, and the strict step would prove J J ≐ void); here the same row at A = J has a void receipt — the instance (J J) is exactly one, so [(J J)] reads ω, which is the value of J J — and proves [<(J)>] ≃ J J, i.e. [<<o>>]… [o] ≃ J J, which is J1.half-period read backwards: the turn is not lost in this row but at the log of one, [o], which 𝕁₁ never erases. It is not strict — the step is witnessed by position whatever its value — and the posted receipt, where it is not void, is exactly the information the classical setting had to legislate about. The group/torsor picture: [()] = ω generates the lattice (unity, with an identity); [<()>] = J is a base point of the coset J + Λ (negation, with none).

Confirms

The depth-1 criterion: a 2πi error is harmless exactly where an exp will swallow it. On the trunk this is every by position guard, now an absorbed receipt — C.period-absorption, Q.reciprocal-of-negative, the seam steps of C.de-moivre — and the trunk's tapes list them (census/j1-ledger.md). What 𝕁₁ does not dissolve: a unit step under a square before any instance. There ≃ does not pass (a lattice offset inside a log is not a lattice offset of the log), so the step is sound only when its receipt is void, which only the reading can see; the classical by content guards under squares survive into 𝕁₁ as imports (alg.power-of-base, alg.sqrt4, C.i-to-the-i and five more) — sound at the generic points of their domains, and five of them (alg.power-of-power, alg.root-of-product, alg.root-of-quotient, C.root-of-negative, C.modulus-of-polar) with a non-void receipt at the exceptional points where a content is exactly one and the square reads ω, named on their tapes: there the reading says √1 = −1 (J1.receptacle at n = 2) and the classical law is false. The gap mult.seam-signature is therefore closed for positions inside instances and at depth 0, and remains open — as a receipt check performed by the reading — under squares.

DECLARATION — the empty square □ = [] is read by polarity: inside an instance it is ✠ (concession: (A □) ≡ void, strictly); outside it is Ω, the log of nothing, already the whole coset −∞ + Λ; a unit step on pole-valued content has no winding to record and posts no receipt — Dominion □ A ≡ □ is strict

GAP — in which contexts is A <A> void and in which a period? The legislation of 2026-08-22 says annihilation is stratified; the strata are not yet a rule of the three-boundary calculus

Confirms

That the stratification is real: in the universal cover of ℂ×, two lifts of the same point differ by a lattice element, so "the same number twice" is ambiguous exactly at the log level and nowhere else. And that it is where J1.pole lives: [A <A>] is the pole □ when the annihilation went to void and [ω], a finite number, when it went to period — "the fork IS the object" (legislation 2026-08-22). It is not a defect of Inversion as an axiom of forms: A <A> with A one and the same form is void in every reading; the question is about two occurrences that the page writes alike.

The ℂ reading is a model of 𝕁₁

the compositional ℂ reading — the log of exactly one is 2πi, every other log principal — satisfies the strict rules exactly at every position (counit, Distribution, Inversion, the hole rules, closure), the unit mod Λ with receipt minus the winding, and absorption exactly; so 𝕁₁ is consistent, and ω ≠ void in it
exp ∘ ln = id; ln ∘ exp = id mod 2πi; e^{z + 2πi} = e^z; 2πi ≠ 0

Everything 𝕁₁ says is true of complex numbers, once you let the log of 1 be 2πi instead of 0. So 𝕁₁ cannot contradict itself, and ω is really there.

Consistency. By induction on derivations, with the position rule of SPEC §5.5: a strict rule applied at any position preserves exact equality of values (the reading is compositional); a witnessed rule applied directly inside an instance preserves the instance's value exactly (e^{a + kω} = e^a); applied at depth 0 it preserves equality mod Λ; under a square it is not applied, since ≃ does not pass through [ ] — except a theorem (a lemma table, a schema's hypothesis) whose own tape is strict or absorbed: by the induction hypothesis its two sides are equal in value everywhere, so it applies like a strict rule at any position, squares included (SPEC §5.5, LEGISLATION 30a). Any other step under a square is an import, which fails a 𝕁₁ node and makes a trunk cell guarded, outside this induction. So the two ends of every derivation are equal, or equal mod Λ, in the model; () ≡ void would need 1 = 0 and () ≃ void would need 1 ∈ 2πiℤ, and neither is derivablemult.c-readingthe same argument as mult.consistency, with the decree replaced by the receipt and the position rule

It is not completeness: that every true congruence mod Λ is derivable is a different and open question (the exp–log identity problem). And it is not a syntactic consistency proof (confluence and termination of the rewrite system); that is the completion pass the ledger of J1.annihilation still owes.

The ψ-wall

WELL-FORMEDNESS — at level k, the fraction ω/n = ([ω] <[n]>) is well formed iff it is ψ-fixed mod Λ: (ψʳ − 1)(ω/n) ∈ Λ for every r coprime to n, where ψʳ is the cardinality power — i.e. iff n divides r^{2k} − 1 for all such r
ψʳ(ω) = rω (wind r times); at weight 2k, ψʳ acts as r^{2k}; ω/n survives iff n | r^{2k} − 1 for all r coprime to n, i.e. λ(n) | 2k (Carmichael)

Not every slice of the circle passes the wall: ω/n passes at level k only if winding it r times, for every r sharing no factor with n, brings it back up to whole turns. The slices that pass are counted by 24, 240, 504.

Derivation

none — adjoined, as a well-formedness decree on the forms ([ω] <[o^{n}]>) of J1.receptacle, built from the cardinality power (mult.cardinality, schema.power) and the lattice (J1.period-form). The content it legislates over is native; what is legislated is the selection: that only the ψ-fixed fractions are in the arithmetic.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The image of J: the ψ-wall at level k selects the n with λ(n) | 2k, and the largest of them is the denominator of B_{2k}/4k — the order of im J in π_{4k−1} (J1.von-staudt-clausen, an import). The chart's cardinality power is the Adams operation ψʳ with its K-theory grading read as winding — the point of the July session was that the grading need not be imported. It is not yet im J as a module (products like η³ = 12ν as forms need Ext¹ data — O1 of the July set), and it is not a theorem: it is a rule about which forms count, and it carries the price of a decree. Which weights 2k are realized (the 4k − 1 pattern) is also still imported.

The places of ℚ are the primes and ∞

IMPORT — every nontrivial absolute value on ℚ is equivalent to |·|_∞ or to one |·|_p (Ostrowski 1916): the chart's places are exactly the pages this rung draws, and no other
the Berkovich spectrum of ℤ: the trivial point at the centre, an archimedean branch, and one branch for each prime — each branch the powers |·|^ε of one absolute value

There are exactly two kinds of place to do arithmetic: the usual one, and one for each prime. Nothing else. That fact has a name and a proof, and the chart borrows both.

none — an import, adjoined before the pages: it names the places the reading at ∞ (mult.c-reading) does not see — one for each prime, each the pile of that many marks (N.numeral) declared void. The proof is the classification of absolute values by whether |n| ≤ 1 for all integers n (non-archimedean: then |·| is some |·|_p) or not (archimedean: then |·| is a power of |·|_∞).

It is not ℤ_p: the whole p-adic integer is the compatible tower of pages at every depth, which the chart's finite page does not contain (place.completion). It is not a new boundary: no fourth boundary is drawn; a pile is declared void, as James's own exclusions declare a form absent.

The reading at a place

DECLARATION — at the place p, to depth n, a form is read in the log space ℤ_p ⊕ ℚ·[p] ⊕ ℚ·J_p: a number part (a residue mod p^n), a count of the prime's log [p], a count of the torsion log J_p; the square of a number splits it into the three counts, the instance of a triple is a number when the number part is in the radius and the counts are whole
a = p^v · τ · u: valuation v, Teichmüller τ = g^k, principal unit u; log a = log u + v·[p] + k·J_p; exp converges on p·ℤ_p (4ℤ_2)

At a finite place a number is a residue on a clock face, and its log is three counts: how often p divides it, which root of unity it points at, and the log of the rest.

The witness checks its claims on random residues at p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 13: the counit ([A]) ≐ A exact; the three counts reassemble A; the period reads as declared and is absorbed.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The p-adic logarithm and exponential (Hensel), the Teichmüller lift, the decomposition ℤ_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1 + pℤ_p): the standard analysis of a local field, read off a page. It is not ℚ_p: the reciprocal of the prime is not a form (place.no-inverse-of-the-prime), so the page is ℤ_p's, and the numbers with a negative count of [p] wait for a decree that admits them. It is not ℂ_p either: only the roots of unity that are forms at p exist there (place.selection); i at p = 3 is not a form, and no extension of the page is drawn.

Refuted readings

"⟨⟩ is the uniformizer at p" — refuted 2026-09-13: the mirror gives J at every place; size lives in [p], the log of the uniformizer p — [oo] at 2. "every p-adic number is a re-entry" — refuted 2026-09-19: finite re-entry systems are countable and ℤ_p is not; completion enters as a rule (place.completion).

Notes

The chart's domains are read at a place by a dictionary (SPEC §4.4): a positive variable is a principal unit, now and then times p or p² — the place's image of the positive reals, the sector where the log is single-valued and every receipt is void (J1.regime-split); negative is minus a principal unit; real either; complex is any residue of the page; natural a small count; unit any unit; and a positive or real variable is a fraction of principal units a fifth of the time, so that a count that is not whole is sampled (the turn laws that hold only for integer turns are told apart there). The exceptional points are probed as at ∞ — a variable exactly one, and minus one for a negative variable. The radius is the standing proviso of every instance at a finite place, not a failure of a law: the ledger retries a sample on the radius and otherwise drops it, unjudged.

The engine checks the law on random units at every instance of the range (p = 2, 3, 5, 7; n = 1, 2); the counting argument behind it — the order of an element divides the order of the group — is what the chart cannot yet make, and the import is its price. A law over the place p rests on place.ostrowski.

It is not a statement about which units have which order (the primitive roots): the torsion log's generator is chosen by the reading (place.reading).

Confirms

Base-p positional notation, James's own number formats (the thesis's Appendix A.3, p. 70: a numeral in any base is a nest of products), and the p-adic digits of Hensel. It is not yet the infinite doll: a finite form has finitely many shells, and the limit — the doll with a shell at every depth, ℤ_p — is the gap place.completion. It is not canonical either: the law allows k ≥ p, and the carry (p marks in one shell are one mark in the next) is the law read at k = p.

Confirms

The Teichmüller lift and the structure ℤ_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1 + pℤ_p): the torsion of the units is the set of Frobenius-fixed points, and it is generated by the instance of J_p. Beside J1.receptacle (every fraction of the period, instanced, is a root of unity) it says which fractions survive at p: those whose power p is themselves — the selection rule in its native form (place.selection). It is not the p-adic log of τ being J_p: the log of a root of unity converges to 0 in ℚ_p; J_p is the formal count the reading keeps, which is why J "survives only formally, as a pure phase" at p (JP ledger).

Refuted readings

"Teichmüller = the ψ-fixed point defines the torsion, for every ψ^r" — refuted 2026-09-13: only the Frobenius ψ^p fixes the torsion; at p = 2, ψ² sends −1 to 1 and kills J; the Adams ψ^r for r ∈ ℤ_p^× fixes nothing at weight 0.

Notes

The schema runs at the odd places 3, 5, 7; at p = 2 the torsion is ±1 = <o> and ω_2 = J J: the (p−1)-th fraction of the period is the period itself, and the law is the closure. The law holds at ∞ too — the engine reads each instance at its own p, so the J1 cell is by hand: the same derivation, with ∞'s period. What is the place's and not ∞'s is the content of the torsion: at ∞ every root of unity is Frobenius-fixed for its own prime, at p only the (p−1)-th roots exist to be fixed (place.selection).

The torsion log J_p

J_p := [T], T a generating Teichmüller element: J := [<o>] ≐ ω_p/2 at every place
J_p = log of a generator of μ_{p−1}, formal (the p-adic log of a root of unity is 0); ω_p = (p−1)·J_p; J = (p−1)/2 · J_p = ω_p/2; at p = 2 the torsion of ℤ_2^× is ±1 (not a Teichmüller lift: μ_1 is trivial there), J_2 = [<o>] and ω_2 = 2·J_2

Minus one has no logarithm at a finite place — but it still needs one, or (J) would stop being −1. So the place keeps J as a count: half a turn, with the whole turn being the period of the place.

The same wall at every place

(ω A) ≃ (A) with ω := [()] at every place v, ω_v the period of v: 2πi at ∞, (p−1)·J_p at an odd p, 2·J_2 at 2 — the same law, the same shape, the same tape

The rule that a whole turn disappears inside a circle is not a fact about the complex numbers. It is a fact about circles and boxes, and it holds at every prime with that prime's own whole turn.

Chapter 9 of the JP ledger, Axiom 4 (Wall), and the 2026-09-13 finding that "the wall has the same shape at every place": verified here by the same prover running at the places. The two closures of Chapter 9 — the void pile on the page, the period inside the instance — sit on opposite sides of Involution: one is declared on the additive layer at depth 0, the other is absorbed at depth 1. It is not the adelic page: one engine runs at one place at a time; the product formula that binds the places is place.local-wall's, for the ψ-wall, and the full adelic form is owed (ROADMAP: J2).

Confirms

That the log space at a finite place is ℤ_p ⊕ ℤ[p] ⊕ ℤJ_p with no finite pole: every finite count of [p] is a legitimate log, and the valuation axis is a line with the pole beyond its upper end. The three laws of mult.black-hole and the two exclusions hold at the pole of the place as at ∞'s (the ledger: mult.hole-exclusion holds everywhere). It is not the other end: the negative counts of [p] are not the pole but legitimate logs whose instances the page refuses (place.no-inverse-of-the-prime, place.two-ends).

Confirms

The convergence of the geometric series in ℚ_p and the doll of a rational number: the rationals are exactly the eventually periodic dolls, the re-entrant ones (JP ledger, EXACT), and this is the simplest, with every digit 1. It is not the limit itself: the law is at depth n, and the infinite doll is the compatible tower of these, the gap place.completion. It is not a convergence at ∞: there the same unfolding repels (1, 3, 7, 15, …), and at an odd prime other than p the form o ([oo][x]) is neutral — 2 is a unit there and nothing shrinks. The place supplies the guard.

Notes

The schema runs at p = 3 to depths 1 … 3 and at p = 2 to depths 2, 3 (at depth 3 the sum has three terms and the telescope two cancellations); the derivation is the same at every p and n, and the prover licenses each instance row by row. At p = 2, depth 1, the law is true (the one-term sum, 1 ≡ −1 mod 2) but not by this derivation: 1 − p is −1 there, not a principal unit, and the page step at the square [o <(oo)>] → [o] changes the square's value by half a period, J₂, which no instance absorbs — the prover grades it absent, and the instance is left out of the range. The guard — "[p] shrinks" — is semantic: it is the void pile acting through place.prime-power, not a rule of its own (the JP ledger's load-bearing gap, paid here by the void pile and its discipline, LEGISLATION 31(g)).

place.two-endsdecreeNATIVE-BY-DECREEhandmetaneed-ledband beyonddeclaration○

The two ends of the page

DECLARATION — the count of [p] has two ends: upward, past every depth, the pole □₊, the log of nothing, which no finite count is (a finite count n·[p] is a log whose instance is the void pile); downward, the negative counts, legitimate logs whose instances — the reciprocals of the prime — are not forms. The page houses one end; a form that houses both — a wheel — is not drawn
+∞·[p] = the pole, the limit of n·[p] as the depth grows (p^n ≐ void at depth n, for every n); −∞·[p] = 1/p^∞, excluded; at ∞ the ends are swapped: −∞ is the pole and +∞ diverges

A number line at a finite place has a top you approach but never reach (nothing) and a bottom you cannot go below (dividing by p). At ∞ it is the other way round. No page gets both ends; that would be a wheel.
