none — a declaration, the place's half of J1.pole. The two ends are already on the chart: the upper end as the limit of place.prime-power (the instance of n·[p] void at depth n, for every n), the lower end as place.no-inverse-of-the-prime; what this node declares is that they are the two ends of one axis, that the pole is the limit and not a finite count, and that the ban on the wheel is kept. The first draft said "past the depth the count is the pole, □₊ = N·[p]"; the referee's chain (2026-10-06) refuted that — a finite count that is the pole collapses the page — and the decree now places the pole beyond every depth.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The projective line's two points at the valuation: ℤ_p has the pole (as the limit of pⁿ → 0) and excludes 1/p; ℚ_p has both, and is the wheel's value reading — the field in which the page's one-endedness is given up for inverses. It is not a claim that ℚ_p is forbidden: it is a claim that it is not this page, and that the decree admitting the other end — a lens, or a second page — is owed (place.completion). It is not a claim that a finite count of [p] is ever the pole: "finite N·[p] = □ in ℤ/p^N" (the JP ledger's rung-count axis, 2026-09-13) is refuted — see place.prime-power.

place.lifttheoremNATIVEenginemetaneed-ledband beyond○

A root at depth one lifts to every depth

for a unit A at an odd place p: (([[A]] <[oo]>)) is a form at p iff A is a square mod p; the Newton step X ↦ ([X ([A] <[X]>)] <[oo]>) doubles the depth at which X² ≐ A
Hensel's lemma for x² = a: a root mod p with 2x a unit lifts uniquely to ℤ_p; Newton's iteration converges quadratically — the depths 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32

To find a square root at a finite place, find one on the clock with p hours; then Newton's step fixes twice as many digits each time. If there is no root on the small clock, there is none at the place at all.

Confirms

Hensel's lemma in its first case and the quadratic residues: a unit is a square in ℤ_p iff it is a square mod p (odd p). It is not the general lemma (f'(x₀) a unit, for any polynomial): the chart has the square root as a form and the rest as the quadratic formula's JP guard (C.quadratic-formula). It is not p = 2, where a unit is a square iff it is ≡ 1 mod 8 and the root form's radius says so (SPEC §4.4; place.radius).

Notes

The chart's earlier JP guard on alg.sqrt4 ("the p-adic log of 2 must converge") was too strong a worry and the wrong one: the log of any unit converges after the torsion is split off; the obstruction is the torsion count's parity. At p = 3, 4 is a principal unit (4 ≡ 1 mod 3) and the root form reads the principal unit whose square is 4, which is −2 (−2 ≡ 1 mod 3): canonical, whatever the generator — the principal root is canonical on the principal units. For a unit that is not principal the root form halves a torsion count, and which of the two halves it takes depends on the reading's choice of generator (the least primitive root, LEGISLATION 31(h)): there the root form picks a root by convention (alg.sqrt4, place.reading).

place.local-walltheoremNATIVEenginemetaneed-ledband beyond○

The wall is the product of its local factors

M(2k) = ∏_p p^{e_p(k)}, with e_p(k) the largest e such that λ(p^e) divides 2k — the ψ-wall at level k is decided one place at a time
e_p(k) = 1 + v_p(k) for odd p with (p−1) | 2k, else 0; e_2(k) = 3 + v_2(k); the product is the denominator of B_{2k}/4k

The number 24 is 8 times 3 because the wall at level 1 is 8 at the place 2 and 3 at the place 3, and nothing anywhere else. Every wall number is built this way, one prime at a time.

classical replacedJ1 holdsJH untestedJO untestedJP holdsC EXACTfinset untestedlambda untestedCC untestedlogic untested
Derivation
statementrulenote
The wall splits. λ(n)2k iff λ(p^e)2k for every p^e ∥ n, since λ(n) = lcm of the λ(p^e); so the largest n with λ(n)2k is the product over p of the largest p^e with λ(p^e)2kJ1.psi-wallCarmichael's function is a least common multiple over the prime powers
The local count. λ(p^e) = (p−1)p^{e−1} for odd p, so λ(p^e)2k iff (p−1)2k and e − 1 ≤ v_p(k): e_p = 1 + v_p(k) when (p−1)2k, else 0. At 2: λ(2) = 1, λ(4) = 2, λ(2^e) = 2^{e−2} for e ≥ 3, so e_2 = 3 + v_2(k)place.selectionthe torsion at p is the (p−1)-th roots of unity (place.teichmuller); its order must divide 2k for ψ^r to fix ω/p^e
The product. ∏_p p^{e_p(k)} = M(2k) = 24, 240, 504, 480, 264, 65520, 24, 16320 for k = 1 … 8J1.wall-censuswitness: computed locally, compared with the census
Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

Von Staudt–Clausen's theorem (1840) read locally: a prime p divides the denominator of B_{2k} iff (p−1) | 2k, with the exact power of p in the denominator of B_{2k}/4k given by J. C. Adams (1878) — the e_p(k) above; and the "universal 24" of the J-tower: every im-J order is divisible by 8·3, because the place 2 contributes 2³ at every level (e_2 = 3 + v_2(k) ≥ 3) and the place 3 contributes 3 at every level (2 | 2k always, so e_3 ≥ 1). It is not a derivation of the labelling M(2k) = |im J| (J. F. Adams, 1965), which stays the rung's import (J1.von-staudt-clausen). It is not the adelic form on one page: the places are read one at a time, and an integer is factored, not a product formula proved.

induction

The first gap. An equational calculus has no "for every pile"; the plan is a meta-move — the finite-set reading, where induction is the universal property of the free monoid on one point. Since rung schema the gap is priced rather than only named: a schema states a law for every n as a template, the engine checks it at every n in a declared range and checks that the hypothesis row is the law at a smaller n, and the passage to all n — the step no engine check reaches — is the gap, cited in that row and carried in the price.

trigonometry

Cosine and sine are defined from the phase — half the sum, and half the difference over i, of a turn and its reverse — and Euler's formula is then the theorem that the two halves reassemble the turn. No lengths, no triangles: the angle is a count of J, in half-turns. The Pythagorean identity and the angle-addition formulas are theorems of the rung (C.pythagorean, C.cosine-addition, C.sine-addition).

zero

Zero has three faces in the calculus: the void (nothing written), the instance of the black hole (□) (zero as a value), and the mirror of nothing <>. The chart keeps them as three laws because the extensions treat them differently.

Gapsconcepts without a form; each carries a plan

N.induction Induction on a pile — GAP — 'a law that holds of void and is preserved by adjoining o holds of every pile' is not a form and not an equation
N.order Order — m < n — GAP — 'oo < ooo' is not a form; order is a predicate on normal forms, not an equation
mult.seam-signature A native signature for the seam — GAP — the calculus cannot say in its own terms which contents are off the principal strip, so the seam discipline has to be stated in the ℂ reading
Q.lowest-terms Lowest terms — a canonical fraction — GAP — 'the reduced form of a fraction' is not an equation: deciding it needs a greatest common divisor, which is an iteration
alg.irrationality Irrationality — √2 is not a fraction — GAP — '(([[oo]] <[oo]>)) is not ≐ any fraction of piles' is a negative statement about all derivations, and the calculus has no form for it
alg.non-radical Algebraic numbers that radicals cannot reach — GAP — no radical form reaches the real root of x⁵ − x − 1 (Abel–Ruffini); whether any form at all does is open: the forms' values are Chow's exp–log numbers, and 'no non-radical algebraic number is an exp–log number' is Chow's conjecture, a theorem only under Schanuel's conjecture (Chow 1999)
J1.annihilation The strata of annihilation — GAP — in which contexts is A <A> void and in which a period? The legislation of 2026-08-22 says annihilation is stratified; the strata are not yet a rule of the three-boundary calculus
place.completion The limit of the pages is not yet a form — GAP — ℤ_p is the compatible tower of the pages at every depth; the chart has the pages and not the tower: a doll with a shell at every depth, a re-entry's limit, and the lens that reads a form to n shells as a form of its own are all owed

Refuted readingskept, struck through, attached to the law they were mistaken for

N.freeness
  • "nothing added later ever collapses two piles" follows from soundness in ℂ — the first draft (2026-10-03) made this claim here with an engine badge; the referee pass the same day showed the unrestricted laws do collapse the calculus unless the undefined forms are excluded, and that nothing in the engine checks a meta claim. Moved to mult.consistency, with its decree and import made explicit.
Z.inversion
  • < > is the uniformizer at a finite place — refuted 2026-09-13: the mirror gives J at every place; the uniformizer at p = 2 is [oo] (p-adic-wall thread).
mult.involution
  • the tower [[[A]]] ≃ [[A]] stabilizes — refuted 2026-08-22 (collapse theorem: with ()-congruence it forces total transparency); stabilization relocated to the mixed closure [(−)] at depth 1.
mult.black-hole
  • □ is +∞ — Lui confirmed 2026-09-13 that □ is log 0 = −∞ when the engine labelled its valuation +∞; the sign depends on which axis (value or valuation) is meant.
mult.hole-instance
  • needs Distribution as well as Involution — the first draft (2026-10-03) derived this through a Distribution detour; the referee pass the same day pointed out it is Involution-up at A = void in one step. Price corrected.
mult.dominion
  • Dominion is a theorem of Involution and Distribution alone — refuted 2026-10-03 by the 3-element model in tools/models/dominion_models.py (mult.dominion-independence).
mult.hole-exclusion
  • [□] is merely an open form, unread but admissible — refuted 2026-10-03 (referee pass): admitting it collapses the calculus by the derivation above. It is excluded, and Bricken's reading of [[ ]] as complex infinity is a reading of an excluded form, not a law.
  • the decree bans only the literal string <□> — refuted the same day: any form ≐ □ (e.g. [J J] once J-cancellation is available at rung C) would bypass a literal ban; the decree is up to ≐.
mult.seam-decree
  • the guard need only cover the orientation [(X)] → X — the first statement of this decree (2026-10-03); refuted the same day by the alg referee pass: the collapse runs backwards through X → [(X)] (Notes).
  • the pilot's rungs need no guard on Involution-down; the J-discipline is rung C's business — refuted 2026-10-03 (second referee pass): J J = [<o>][<o>] is writable at rung mult, and the collapse above uses only rungs ≤ Q.
  • "phased" — a square with an angle somewhere inside it — is a sufficient syntactic signature for off-strip content, so the decree can be stated in forms alone — refuted the same day by the consistency witness (tools/models/consistency_check.py): [[[oo]]] = ln(ln ln 2) has imaginary part π with no angle anywhere, and [[[oo]]] [[[oo]]] is off the strip. Sign is lost under iterated squares, not only under mirrors; which iterated squares lose it depends on values ([[ooo]] is positive, [[oo]] negative). The decree is therefore semantic, and its nativity is the gap mult.seam-signature.
mult.seam-signature
  • "phased" (a square with an angle inside) is the signature — refuted 2026-10-03 by [[[oo]]]; recorded at mult.seam-decree.
mult.consistency
  • the unrestricted equational theory of the pilot's laws is consistent — refuted 2026-10-03 (first referee pass). Route A: with [□] admitted, W = (o [□]) satisfies W ≐ W (o [C]) by Dominion-under-square and Distribution, so Inversion gives (o [C]) ≐ void for every C, hence o ≐ void.
  • Route B needs rung C (a named J) — refuted the same day (second referee pass): J J = [<o>][<o>] is writable at rung mult; one unguarded unit step gives J J ≐ void, and the ℚ sign rules finish the collapse (recorded at mult.seam-decree). The first draft of this node deferred the guard to rung C; it is needed from rung mult on.
Q.negative-fraction
  • a/(−b) = −(a/b) follows "by the same promotion with the roles exchanged" — the first draft (2026-10-03) claimed this in prose; the referee pass the same day showed no instantiation of inverse promotion matches ([A] <[<B>]>). The bottom-sign law is Q.negative-denominator and needs Q.reciprocal-of-negative.
Q.rational
  • every form in which each pile occurs only as [pile] or <[pile]> directly under an instance is rational — refuted 2026-10-03 (second referee pass): (([oo])) = e² fits that description. The class must be stated as juxtapositions of (mirrored) instances of such contents.
alg.non-radical
  • Lehmer's number is a radical form — refuted 2026-10-01 in the exp–log thread: the Galois group of its degree-5 trace polynomial is S₅, so the Galois group of the degree-10 Lehmer polynomial is not solvable. (The first record here said "is a form" and "Galois group S₅" of the Lehmer polynomial itself; both corrected 2026-10-03 — the group of the degree-10 polynomial lies in C₂ ≀ S₅ and is larger than S₅.)
  • the real root of x⁵ − x − 1 is not ≐ any form — overclaimed 2026-10-03 and corrected the same day: Abel–Ruffini excludes radical forms only; the exp–log case is Chow's conjecture.
C.phase-independence
  • phase independence holds for every form A — James's statement of Theorem 1 (p. 44, "For all A ∈ B"); refuted 2026-10-03 at A = J (and at every A with Im a outside (−2π, 0]): the proof's last step is the seam step. Its consequence J J ≐ void is struck at C.double-phase.
C.log-of-negative
  • [<A>] ≐ [A] J holds for every form A (the on-sight rule as a law) — refuted 2026-10-03 (alg referee pass) at A = [[oo]]; recorded at mult.seam-decree and C.james-discipline.
C.double-phase
  • J J ≐ void — James's J-cancellation stated without its instance; refuted as a depth-0 law 2026-10-03 (its content is 2πi; the collapse it causes is recorded at mult.seam-decree, its restatement in James's terms at C.james-discipline).
C.phase-sign
  • J ≐ <J> — false on the bare page (iπ ≠ −iπ); only its instance holds. Refuted 2026-10-03 as a step of the collapse route (mult.seam-decree).
C.james-discipline
  • the J-discipline and the seam decree are the same rule — the first statement of this node (2026-10-03, same day); refuted by its own body in the C referee pass: the decree adjudicates non-J seam steps and the Involution route to the crack, which the J-rules do not, and rule 1 as stated is false off the lower half-plane. Struck, and the node restated as an inclusion.
  • the J-discipline is a convention about a special symbol J, separate from the axioms — it is a special case of the admissibility condition on the unit step of mult.involution, which the chart states before J is named (an interpretive thesis, recorded rather than witnessed).

The refutations of J J ≐ void and J ≐ <J> as depth-0 laws, and of the on-sight rule for every A, live at C.double-phase, C.phase-sign and C.log-of-negative respectively.

J1.regime-split

< >-free forms are Λ-free (T4 as stated, 2026-07-21) — refuted 2026-10-04 by [(ω ω)] and [([[[oo]]] [[[oo]]])], witness tools/models/j1_regime.py.

place.void-pile

"([p]^∞ [Z]) ≡ void is a new p-adic axiom" — refuted 2026-09-13: it is the black hole, (□) ≐ void, which the chart already has (mult.hole-instance); the void pile is the only new declaration.

place.reading

"⟨⟩ is the uniformizer at p" — refuted 2026-09-13: the mirror gives J at every place; size lives in [p], the log of the uniformizer p — [oo] at 2. "every p-adic number is a re-entry" — refuted 2026-09-19: finite re-entry systems are countable and ℤ_p is not; completion enters as a rule (place.completion).

place.prime-log

"the mirror ⟨⟩ is the uniformizer" — refuted 2026-09-13: the mirror gives J at every place and has zero count of [p]; size is [p]'s alone.

place.teichmuller

"Teichmüller = the ψ-fixed point defines the torsion, for every ψ^r" — refuted 2026-09-13: only the Frobenius ψ^p fixes the torsion; at p = 2, ψ² sends −1 to 1 and kills J; the Adams ψ^r for r ∈ ℤ_p^× fixes nothing at weight 0.

place.prime-power

"[o^{p}]^{n} ≐ □: n copies of [p] are the pole at depth n" — refuted 2026-10-06 (the place referee pass): with the void pile usable under a square the law derives o^{5} ≐ void at p = 5, depth 2, and makes juxtaposition non-associative in the reading (−[p] + [p] + [p] grouped two ways). The pole is the limit end; the finite count is this law.

place.geometric-doll

"every p-adic number is a re-entry" — refuted 2026-09-19: finite re-entry systems are countable; completion must enter as a rule (place.completion).

place.two-ends

"past the depth the count of [p] is the pole: □₊ = N·[p]" — refuted 2026-10-06 by the place referee's chain (o^{5} ≐ void at p = 5, depth 2): a finite count that is the pole makes the page inconsistent. The pole is the limit end.

place.completion

"every p-adic number is a re-entry" — refuted 2026-09-19.
